title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
statement: For admissible origins, π(N(A)) is the intrinsic affine-induced Specht module S(A): its jth column contributes the Specht shape read from its nonnegative ground differences and evaluation at a_j=c_j+q_j−n, and the factors are induced along the affine Young subalgebra. π(K(A))=D(A) is simple for A∈Std and zero otherwise; Std labels give all distinct simples of the relevant Hecke image. For A∈Std, π(P(A)) is its projective cover Y(A) and π*π(P(A))=P(A). All ambient offStd projectives still have their genuine images, without a false projective-preservation assertion. Tilting images have the actual opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag coefficients, and π is fully faithful on tiltings. For B∈Std, [S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):K(B)]=d_(B,A)(1), using the actual typed singular/parabolic coefficient conventions; B offStd is not a simple Hecke label. All these interfaces are ungraded at parameter1.
strategy: Assume AC and work over C. In a stable realization choose d distinct full ground rows; their regular graded Hecke vector gives the rank-one weight idempotent e_S and identifies Hom_W(M,−) with e_S(−). Its generators are row permutations and h(x_i)=e_S(−D_(n−d+i)^(2)+e2(c)+e1(c)+d−n−i+1)e_S. The canonical colour fibre of a finite Levi standard is the tensor product of the column Specht modules by ordinary Schur–Weyl; these corner x_i act as a_j plus their within-column Jucys sums. Row permutations generate the other colour fibres, and multinomial dimensions prove the intrinsic induced-Specht isomorphism. This replaces the false source equality with Hom_p, not a definition of S(A) by π. The cyclic highest-vector proof identifies W types and the stable enlargement/contractible corner extends the conclusion to the original pyramid. Exact quotient/Morita proves the simple claim; add(T) recovery and full-projective FF give the cover claim for Std. Apply exact π to the actual16 tilting standard flag and its typed multiplicity dictionary. Exactness gives the restricted-B comparison. Specht-corner §§1–4 contains the explicit corner/evaluation calculations.
